title: Apply Resource Protection
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 7: Security Operations: Apply Resource Protection.

items: Media lifecycle: creation → use → storage → transportation → disposal
Marking/labeling — media must be labeled with its classification level
Handling — follow classification-specific handling procedures (e.g., top secret media requires different handling than public media)
Storage — store in access-controlled areas appropriate to classification; portable media (USB, tapes) in locked safes or vaults
Transportation — use tamper-evident packaging; maintain chain of custody during transport
Sanitization — clearing, purging, or destruction (covered in Domain 2)
Downgrading — reducing the classification level of media; some organizations prohibit downgrading entirely (e.g., top secret media is destroyed, never downgraded)
Backup tapes should be protected as confidential information at minimum

blocks.text: Media management extends to all forms of data storage: hard drives, USB drives, optical media, backup tapes, and even paper documents. Each type requires appropriate handling throughout its lifecycle. Tape media is highly susceptible to loss due to corruption, physical damage, and theft. Basic physical security practices should be followed: storing tapes in locked safes or vaults, or within a secure room with additional physical security controls. When media is being decommissioned, the sanitization method must match the classification level. For government environments, the US government doesn't consider any purging method acceptable to purge top secret data — media labeled top secret will always remain top secret until it is physically destroyed. rows: ❌ NOT effective — SSDs have no magnetic media

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: Degaussing does NOT work on SSDs — SSDs use flash memory, not magnetic platters. For SSDs: use crypto-erase (if self-encrypting drive) or physical destruction. See Domain 2 for detailed sanitization coverage.

items: Asset inventory — maintain a comprehensive inventory of all hardware and software assets
Track: owner, location, classification, configuration, purchase date, license information, warranty status
Tangible assets — hardware (servers, laptops, network devices); tracked via serial numbers, barcodes, RFID tags
Intangible assets — software licenses, intellectual property, data
Review intangible assets at least annually
Asset management tools can automate discovery and tracking
End-of-life (EOL) and end-of-support (EOS) — track vendor support timelines; unsupported systems are security risks
